chapter_title: Concerning the Form of the Word, that [ ... 30 ... ]
chapter_note: A compact, systematic five-fold correspondence teaching: the production of a word is analyzed through five mouth/throat members, then mirrored by a five-step artisan process (coin-making). Only the opening attribution is later frame; the teaching itself stays in impersonal, mechanical description without institutional application or NT overlay.

paragraphs.core_text: the production of the word t[hat comes] from the mouth and is heard by the [ears]. [ ... ⟨p.261⟩ ... ] and the throat draws it up and the tongue spreads it out and the teeth cut it and the lips g[at]her it! The word shall come forth through the power of th[ese five] members and be heard outside.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the dialogue/frame attribution: "Once again he speaks" and the speech tag "He says" (hagiographic editorial apparatus).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Opens with a formulaic frame marker (“Once again… He says”), but the substance is a five-member mechanistic analysis (impersonal, degree-like enumeration), characteristic of the older correspondential teaching style.

paragraphs.core_text: Simila[rly] the coin: One shall pour it out and an [othe]r beat it and another trim it as it is turned, and a[nother] put the stamp on it and another wipe it in the sieve (?). [Behold], these five craftsmen shall shape and beautify [their] coin, and it comes amongst mankind. It becomes a posse[ssion] to be received and given.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure correspondential analogy structured as a five-fold process (five craftsmen/operations), with no citation formulae, exhortation, or institutional pointing; the mapping remains descriptive and systematic.

paragraphs.core_text: This is also the case with the [wor]d, as it is formed and embellished by five [member]s. It comes forth and is heard by the ears [of] others.
paragraphs.temporal_note: A brief impersonal recapitulation that closes the five-fold mapping; no frame, pastoral address, or overlay markers.
